$comment: The TrueNorth character rig contract, task 1.11. NORMATIVE: assets/style/rig-contract.md is the prose;
this file is the same contract as data, and it is what the contract tests load.
It is authored under assets/ because assets/** is the art agent boundary. content/schemas/rig.schema.json
(ADR-0017) validates this shape and tests/unit/contracts/rig-is-coherent.test.ts reads it from here.
content/characters/rig.json - the path CLAUDE.md names - EXISTS and is a byte-for-byte mirror of this
file except for its $schema, which is relative to content/. The two are edited together, in the same
commit, or the rig has two live copies and no gate can tell you which one is stale.
Every name here appears IDENTICALLY in the Rive file and in the sprite atlas. That identity is the
whole point of ICharacterRenderer: gameplay code must not be able to tell which backend it got.

characterSpace.note: Part windows are given in THIS space, so a window origin IS the part offset. To place a character at world (x, y) with its feet on the ground, draw each part at (x - 120 + frame.x, y - 460 + frame.y). THE VIEW IS PART OF THIS SPACE: every character is drawn three-quarter with the canonical facing RIGHT, about 40 degrees off strict profile toward the viewer, because this is a side-scroller and a figure that faces the camera cannot read as travelling. Screen x is therefore the FORE-AFT axis, which is what makes the walk cycle swing at full amplitude, and the near side is the wearer RIGHT - so the -r parts draw last. See art-bible.md 7.1 and rig-contract.md 1.

artboards.note: Generic constable. Never named as a member of a real force, and the artboard carries no crest, wordmark, collar dog, shoulder flash, chevron or service number.

The beaver guide: the companion who appears at points of interest and leads the learning moments. It plays the SAME rig, the same state machine and the same four expressions as every person in the game, and it stands to the same 6-head canon - costume distinguishes characters, stature never does (art bible 7). `skin`, `hairShape` and `hairColour` fall back like any NPC document and are inert here: `head-shell-beaver` covers the shared head and the short crop entirely, which is why no pelt tone was added to the skin slot. It is a companion animal, never a stand-in for a person: docs/content-review.md applies to it as it does to everything else.

inputs.name: grounded
inputs.meaning: Feet are on the ground polyline.

inputs.name: moving
inputs.meaning: The traversal system wants forward motion (hold-to-move, or auto-move).

inputs.name: talking
inputs.meaning: A dialogue or question card owns this character.

inputs.name: reducedMotion
inputs.meaning: Suppress squash-and-stretch and hold the idle key. Set by the caller from settings; the renderer never reads settings itself.

inputs.name: speed
inputs.meaning: Horizontal speed normalised to this character top speed. Selects walk below 0.55 and run at or above it.

inputs.name: verticalSpeed
inputs.meaning: Vertical velocity normalised: positive rising, negative falling. Only read while grounded is false.

inputs.name: interact
inputs.meaning: Fired when the player taps an NPC or a POI in range.

selector.note: First match wins. This is the Rive state machine written out, and it is exactly what a sprite adapter evaluates - same inputs, same order, same answer. A contract test can drive both backends through this table and compare the selected state.

rules.when: interact fired and its state has not finished
land fired and its state has not finished and not reducedMotion

expressions.note: setExpression(name) resolves the {expression} template variable. Every pose differs in the SHAPE of brow, pupil and mouth, so it survives greyscale, high contrast and the plain Canvas tier, which has no Filter pipeline (ADR-0011).

events.name: footfall
events.when: Each foot plant in walk and run, at t 0.0 and 0.5.
events.use: Step audio and its subtitle equivalent.

events.name: interactReach
events.use: The moment the POI or dialogue opens, so art and UI agree.

events.name: landImpact
events.when: t 0.0 of the land state. Still fired under reducedMotion even though the state is skipped.
events.use: Impact audio, camera shake where enabled.

skin.note: The six ramps ship UNNAMED here: naming is docs/content-review.md 8.1 and OQ-REVIEW-6, not art. fallback is for NPC documents and save recovery only; it is arbitrary (the middle of the ordinal ramp) and the creator never renders it as a pre-selection - it randomises uniformly on open.

costume.note: Not player-selectable, so it is outside the slot-independence product: it says WHICH character this artboard is, not how a player customised one. `beaver` is the guide's pelt, and it drives four parts no human artboard resolves - tail, head-shell, muzzle and the bare hide of the paws and hind feet.

presentation.note: The slot NAME is reserved so the Rive file and the atlas agree when the question is answered. It has no options today and a contract test skips reserved slots. It will be a slot on the one artboard with the one proportion canon - never a second artboard and never a second rig.

slotIndependence.rule: Every option in every slot is available with every option in every other slot.
slotIndependence.checkable: The product of the option counts equals the number of valid combinations; no part frame template names two slots that constrain each other. hairShape and hairColour are separate slots for exactly this reason: one slot of 20 combined options could hide a coupling.

parts.name: tail
parts.note: The guide’s paddle tail. `tail-parka` and `tail-serge` are absent from `frames`, so the part draws nothing on every human artboard - the same mechanism every "none" option uses, and no special case in either backend. Carried out to the wearer’s right, which in a right-facing three-quarter pose is the TRAILING side, so it streams out behind the animal instead of hiding behind its body.

atlas.rule: A part whose resolved template is not in "frames" draws nothing. That is how every "none" option works, and it needs no special case in either backend.
atlas.note: assets/src/svg/shared/character/<name>.svg becomes atlas frame key character-<name> (scripts/assets.mjs, shared owner). The Rive file uses the SAME strings as its slot names.

idle.note: Breathing only: the torso and head rise 1.6 px. The rest pose is a three-quarter stand with the limbs hanging straight, because the mirrored pair cannot hold a stride without crossing over itself - the stride belongs to the walk keys. Under reducedMotion the state holds key 0.

walk.note: A side-scroller walk, solved by forward kinematics from the hip and the shoulder. Screen x is the fore-aft axis in this view, so the swing is horizontal and reads at phone size; the near arm opposes the near leg. Contact at t 0 and t 0.5 is where `footfall` fires.

run.note: The same cycle at 1.45x amplitude and 0.69x duration, with the torso leaning further into the run.

jump-rise.note: Arms and knees in opposite poses, not just an offset: the state has to read on the plain tier, which has no filters.

jump-fall.note: The mirror image of jump-rise at the shoulder and the knee, so rise and fall differ in SHAPE and not in height alone.

land.note: The only squash-and-stretch in the rig: both knees fold and the body drops 12 px. Under reducedMotion this state is skipped entirely and the machine goes straight to the next one, which is why the selector tests it before anything else.

talk.note: The near-side hand comes up and the head tilts. Dialogue text is DOM and carries the words; this state only says WHO is speaking, which is why it is shape and not a glow.

interact.note: The near arm reaches forward, along the direction of travel, so the gesture points at what was tapped.
